preconditions.expression: t == int(stdin.split()[0]) and t >= 1 and t <= 1000
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(3 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::] if line.strip() and int(line.split()[0]) == n)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line after t is an integer n (3 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) representing the number of vertices in the cake.

preconditions.expression: all(len(piece) == 3 and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in piece) for piece in pieces)
preconditions.description: Each of the n-2 lines after n contains three distinct integers a, b, c (1 ≤ a, b, c ≤ n) representing the vertices of a triangular piece, given in random order.
The number of pieces is exactly n-2, where n is the number of vertices in the cake.
Each piece is a valid triangle with three distinct vertices.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in p) and len(p) == n and len(set(p)) == n
postconditions.description: The first line of output for each test case is a permutation p of n distinct integers (1 ≤ p_i ≤ n) representing the vertices of the cake in clockwise or counterclockwise order.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n - 2 for x in q) and len(q) == n - 2 and len(set(q)) == n - 2
postconditions.description: The second line of output for each test case is a permutation q of n-2 distinct integers (1 ≤ q_i ≤ n-2) representing the order in which the pieces were cut.

postconditions.expression: all(vertices_in_piece(pieces[q[i] - 1], p) for i in range(n - 2))
postconditions.description: For each piece in the order q, the vertices of the piece must be three consecutive vertices in the permutation p (considering cyclic order).

postconditions.expression: all(is_valid_cut(p, pieces[q[i] - 1], i) for i in range(n - 2))
postconditions.description: The cutting process must be valid: at each step i, the piece q[i] must be a triangle formed by three consecutive vertices in the current polygon, and the remaining polygon must stay convex.

invariants.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in p) and len(p) == n and len(set(p)) == n
invariants.description: The permutation p must always contain all integers from 1 to n exactly once.

invariants.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n - 2 for x in q) and len(q) == n - 2 and len(set(q)) == n - 2
invariants.description: The permutation q must always contain all integers from 1 to n-2 exactly once.
